solution: The chapter states directly in the 'Do you know?' box on Written Sources: "The place where historical documents are preserved is called 'Archives'. The main office of the National Archives of India is at New Delhi. It is the largest among the Archives in Asia." Pune, Kolkata and Hyderabad are not mentioned in connection with the Archives anywhere in the chapter.

The chapter defines the category verbatim: "Audio-visual sources : Television, films, internet are called 'Audio-visual media'. Many domestic and foreign television channels also come under this head, eg., History channel, Discovery channel, etc." Newspapers and periodicals are listed under Written Sources, and All India Radio is not named among the audio-visual media in the chapter (radio is audio-only, not audio-visual).

This is a 'which is NOT' stem, so the answer is the odd one out. The chapter's Material (physical) sources diagram lists Coins, Places of worship, Royal Seals, Ornaments, Museums, Modern architecture, Things in daily use and Clothing — which covers coins, ornaments and buildings. Proverbs belong to a different category: "Oral sources : These sources include folktales, folksongs, proverbs, ballads and owis."
